source.text: The limit minus the adiabatic peak: 1150 C = 1423.15 K minus 1097.4691 K. The pulse is a few milliseconds from 20 C, so the cladding stays far below 500 C and only the 1150 C rule is in force. A margin is not an integrity assessment: FEED computes no stress.
source.check: Second method: the same peak entry's cross-checks (the SAR's own equation 9 for the steady case; oracles/transient-case-reference.py for the pulse); the margin is that peak subtracted from the limit, and FEED's limit check reports the same number through the real solver (docs/temperature-limits.md).

coverage.domain: TRIGA hot channel, sech^2 pulse built from UT-Austin SAR numbers (illustrative), with the SAR fuel temperature limits
